naturalSplitPoints.title: 23أ — استقرار الحرّاس: السبب المشترك يُسمّى أو يُنفى بالقياس (Stabilise the 17 live guards / name or refute the shared root cause)
contains: Instrument the live matrix so a round is recorded, not remembered: emit a per-guard machine-readable result (pass/fail/timeout, wall time, Chrome boot time, peak concurrency) and commit a rounds ledger file. The 'ten consecutive green rounds' rule in ci.yml:114-116 is unenforceable until this exists.

Test the resource-contention hypothesis directly and cheaply: the matrix currently runs 17 Chrome-launching jobs with unbounded parallelism. Run N rounds with `max-parallel` throttled (e.g. 4) against N rounds unthrottled and compare the buckets. If the ledger collapses toward 4/4 under throttling, the shared cause is named and the fix is one line.

Separate the three guards recorded as failing LOCALLY too — measure · picker · popup (§6 row 97) — from the environment question entirely; these are product/guard bugs and must be triaged as such, not counted as flakiness.

Finish the isolation work commit 9d64625 started: its own message records the picker/measure race still firing at ~35–40% after the armPointer fix, attributing it to a Chromium/CDP internal race (hit-test precedes paint-tree update). Either find the deterministic signal to wait on, or prove none exists and record that in §6.
Flip `blocking: true` for every guard that earns ten consecutive green rounds under the recorder, one line per guard (ci.yml:121-137).
naturalSplitPoints.whyThisBoundary: This is the only item in the whole area whose cause is admitted unknown, and every other Phase 23 deliverable runs ON TOP of these 17 guards. Writing E2E specs, adding a dpr=2 pass, or turning on pixel comparison against an unstable tier produces results nobody can interpret — and dpr=2 in particular doubles guard runtime, which would aggravate the leading hypothesis. It is also the only sub-phase with genuine unknowns: the other three are construction work with known shapes. Per the repo's own §6 row 97, a guard that has never run green in the environment it guards is not a proven guard; 23أ is what converts 17 declared guards into 17 proven ones.
naturalSplitPoints.verifiableBy: Ten consecutive green CI rounds recorded in the committed ledger, with at least the 4/4 set (fullpage · library · overlay) flipped to `blocking: true` in ci.yml and the `continue-on-error` line at 140 doing real work. planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: picker/index.html has two NESTED OPEN shadow roots and no closed one anywhere in the fixture tree; and exactly one iframe, same-origin (`src="/picker/frame.html"`). So picker/ covers roughly half of row 17 and one third of row 18 — and cross-origin is not merely unwritten but structurally impossible today, since fixtures-serve.mjs binds a single origin.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: 'مصفوفة devicePixelRatio: كل سيناريو التقاط يُشغَّل عند dpr = 1 و2' — every capture scenario runs at dpr 1 and 2.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: Zero percent implemented, and no groundwork exists. No verify script sets a device scale factor: the only `--force-device-scale-factor` in the entire scripts/ tree is `=1` in brand-icons.mjs:114, and `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` appears nowhere. Scripts only READ window.devicePixelRatio and hardcode `devicePixelRatio: 1` into seeded IndexedDB records. Every measurement recorded in Phases 8-17 was therefore taken at the runner's native dpr only.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: `grep -rn 'Emulation\.|force-device-scale-factor' scripts/*.mjs` → single hit, brand-icons.mjs:114 with value 1; verify-capture.mjs:302 and verify-fullpage.mjs:518 read dpr; verify-library.mjs:224,229,242 and verify-compare-diff.mjs:236,481,677,810 hardcode devicePixelRatio:1

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: Phase 23 lists 'الانحدار البصري: لقطات مرجعية لكل شاشة إضافة، بعتبة اختلاف صارمة، وخطوط الأساس مثبَّتة في المستودع' — reference shots for every extension screen, strict threshold, baselines committed.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: ci.yml has already decided the opposite, with a reason: lines 191-194 state the eye-comparison is intentional because a pixel baseline on a monthly-changing browser produces more false failures than detections, so shots are UPLOADED and never compared (same for the a11y-tree baselines, lines 204-205). And coverage is thin: 16 baseline files across phase-05/07/08/15/18 only — 5 of 18 closed phases, not 'every extension screen'. Phase 23 must overturn that CI decision with a measurement or narrow its own requirement; it cannot simply implement the plan text as written without contradicting a reasoned decision in the tree.

openQuestions: Has the resource-contention hypothesis ever been tested? The live matrix runs 17 Chrome-launching jobs with no `max-parallel` cap (ci.yml:117-137). If GitHub schedules them concurrently on a shared pool, that is the cheapest candidate explanation for a failure set that moves every round — and one line of YAML would test it. I found no evidence in the repo that this was tried.

The ledger is 4 rounds over 17 guards = 68 observations, and the classification was already refuted at 1 round and again at 3. What N makes the promotion decision safe? The rule says ten consecutive green rounds per guard, but with no recorder (nothing in the repo records per-round results) the count will again rest on memory. Should 23أ's first deliverable be the recorder rather than any fix?

Three guards (measure · picker · popup) are recorded as failing LOCALLY too (§6 row 97), i.e. real bugs, not environment. Were those three ever triaged as product bugs? Commit 9d64625 isolated the picker/measure race and explicitly did NOT fix it (~35–40% recurrence, deferred to Phase 23). Is the local failure of `popup` the same race or a separate, unexamined one?

Does the Phase 23 dependency on Playwright survive contact with known-issues item 2? Playwright's extension support is built on --load-extension, which Chrome 137+ silently disables. If Playwright ends up being only a test runner wrapped around the existing hand-rolled CDP, is the dependency worth its weight versus finishing scripts/lib/cdp.mjs and running the guards under vitest?

Paths أ and د of the four E2E journeys terminate in export (Phase 19) and share (Phase 21), neither started. Should 23ج be scheduled after 21 as ADR 0013's order implies, or should the journeys be written truncated and extended later? The ADR order (…21 → 22 → 23…) already places 23 after both, so this may be answered — but the MVP-gate smoke package (§4 item 4) pulls a slice of 23 BEFORE the gate, and that slice's scope against 19/21 is not specified.

Should the 'stabilise the guards' work be numbered as a Phase 23 sub-phase at all, or pulled forward as its own phase ahead of 19/20أ? The guards currently block nothing (all 17 blocking:false), which means every phase from here to 28 merges with no live-behaviour gate. That is a standing risk that grows with each phase, and the MVP gate is only two phases away.

Does 'حزمة دخان دنيا من المرحلة 23' (§4 item 4, required BEFORE the MVP gate) mean the flakiness must be resolved before the gate? Its text is 'install Playwright, smoke over the fixtures that actually exist, on top of the existing verify scripts' — which is satisfiable with guards still non-blocking. If so, the pre-gate slice proves less than it appears to, and that should be said plainly at the gate rather than discovered after it.
